subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should it be global, per-agent, hostname-scoped, or folded into the broader egress-policy design?
rationale: The lower-level primitive exists, but exposing it changes an SSRF boundary and public config contract; automation cannot choose the metadata/link-local, redirect, cache, provider-fallback, authorization, and audit policy safely without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped Dangerous SSRF Policy
options.body: Land a nested `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design, optionally per-agent, with explicit dangerous naming and hard security semantics for metadata/link-local, redirects, caches, provider fallback, docs, and audit output.

options.title: Keep Current Narrow Opt-Ins
options.body: Leave current main as-is with only fake-IP proxy exceptions and document that arbitrary private-network `web_fetch` remains intentionally unsupported for now.

options.title: Fold Into Egress Policy
options.body: Route this into the broader web-tool egress firewall work so private-network access, domain allowlists, and per-agent authorization are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Dangerous SSRF Policy
recommendation.body: Land a nested `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design, optionally per-agent, with explicit dangerous naming and hard security semantics for metadata/link-local, redirects, caches, provider fallback, docs, and audit output.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the visible policy reviewer on this issue and have the strongest recent history across the guarded-fetch, SSRF, and web_fetch runtime surfaces.
